question: What does the UK offer to its permanent residents or citizens?
options: A right to join in the election of a government
Free access to all national museums
correctAnswers: A right to join in the election of a government
explanation: A right to join in the election of a government is the correct answer.

question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental principle of British life?
options: Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs
explanation: The fundamental principles of British life include: tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs, the rule of law, democracy, individual liberty and participation in community life.

question: What do you need to apply to become a permanent resident or citizen of the UK (choose TWO options)?
options: To be able to speak and read English
A good understanding of life in the UK
correctAnswers: To be able to speak and read English
A good understanding of life in the UK
explanation: The UK offers to its residents or citizens: freedom of belief and religion, freedom of speech, freedom from unfair discrimination, a right to a fair trial and a right to join in the election of a government.

question: What does the UK offer to its residents or citizens (choose FIVE answers)?
options: A right to a fair trial
A right to join in the election of a government
correctAnswers: A right to a fair trial
A right to join in the election of a government
explanation: To apply to become a permanent resident or citizen of the UK, you will need to speak and read English and have a good understanding of life in the UK.

question: Which of the following is a fundamental principle of life in the UK?
options: Intolerance of those with different beliefs
explanation: The fundamental principles of British life include: democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs, and participation in community life.

question: Which TWO of the following responsibilities will you have as a permanent resident or citizen of the UK?
options: To respect and obey the law
To go to church on Sundays
To look after the area in which you live and the environment
correctAnswers: To respect and obey the law
To look after the area in which you live and the environment
explanation: If you wish to be a permanent resident or citizen of the UK, you should respect and obey the law, respect the rights of others, including their right to their own opinions, treat others with fairness, look after yourself and your family and look after the area in which you live and the environment.

question: Participation in community life is a fundamental principle of British life.
explanation: The fundamental principles of British life include: participation in community life.

question: To look after yourself and your family is one of the responsibilities that you will have as a permanent resident or citizen of the UK.
explanation: This statement is TRUE.

question: In which of the following languages is the life in the UK test NOT available?
explanation: The Life in the UK test is usually taken is English, although special arrangements can be made if you wish to take it in Welsh or Scottish Gaelic.

question: Which of the following statements is true?
options: To apply to become a permanent resident or citizen of the UK, you will need to have a university degree
To apply to become a permanent resident or citizen of the UK, you will need to have a good understanding of life in the UK
To apply to become a permanent resident or citizen of the UK, you will need to have British relatives

explanation: To apply to become a permanent resident or citizen of the UK, you will need to have a good understanding of life in the UK and be able to speak and read English.

options: Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs

explanation: There are also several islands which are closely linked with the UK but are not part of it: the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man. These have their own governments and are called ‘Crown dependencies’.
